prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Summary of key proposals (ideology-free)

Economy and investment
- Create a Sustainable Investment Board; launch a £400bn National Transformation Fund, including a £250bn Green Transformation Fund.
- Establish a National Investment Bank with Regional Development Banks and a Post Bank to expand lending, especially to SMEs and communities.
- Tighten financial regulation to shift capital from polluting assets to green investment; change London Stock Exchange listing rules to require climate responsibility.

Climate, energy and industry
- Target most emissions reductions by 2030; create 1m climate jobs.
- Deliver ~90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low-carbon sources by 2030; expand offshore/onshore wind, solar, tidal; retain new nuclear; ban fracking.
- Retrofit almost all homes to high efficiency; roll out heat pumps, district heat networks, storage and grid upgrades.
- Impose a windfall tax on oil firms; support a just transition for energy workers.
- Bring energy and water into public ownership; create a UK National Energy Agency and 14 Regional Energy Agencies.
- Raise R&D to 3% of GDP; support steel, hydrogen, CCS; build gigafactories; develop plastics remanufacturing; green public procurement.

Transport
- Bring rail and buses into public ownership; reinstate cut bus routes; free bus travel for under‑25s where councils control services.
- Nationwide rail electrification; HS2 to Scotland; “Crossrail for the North”; expand rail freight.
- Increase cycling/walking funding; aim to end new combustion car sales by 2030; invest in EV charging and zero‑emission public fleets.

Environment, food and animal welfare
- New Climate and Environment Emergency Bill; Clean Air Act; increased flood defence funding.
- Legally binding nature recovery targets; major tree planting; stronger protected areas; environmental tribunal.
- Producer responsibility for waste; deposit return schemes.
- Establish a Right to Food; halve food bank use in a year and end need in three years; net‑zero food production by 2040.
- Strengthen animal welfare, including ending certain wildlife culls and harmful trapping.

Public finances and services
- Fund services via fairer taxation (higher rates only on top earners; no VAT rise); major anti‑avoidance drive.
- Presumption to insource public services; phase out PFI; £150bn Social Transformation Fund for estates.
- Public sector pay: year‑one 5% rise and above‑inflation increases thereafter.

Health and social care
- Health spending to rise by 4.3% annually; end outsourcing; invest in capital, IT and diagnostics; free prescriptions and basic dentistry.
- Expand mental health access, modernise facilities, boost children’s services.
- Create a National Care Service; free personal care for older people; cap lifetime care costs; improve care worker pay and conditions; raise Carer’s Allowance.

Education and skills
- Sure Start Plus; 30 hours free preschool for all 2–4‑year‑olds; extend paid maternity leave to 12 months.
- More school funding; class sizes capped at 30 in primaries; scrap SATs; arts premium; stronger SEND support.
- Bring academies/free schools under local oversight; free school meals for all primary pupils.
- Lifelong learning entitlements (to Level 3 and six years at Levels 4–6); abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; post‑qualification admissions.
- Climate Apprenticeships funded via reformed levy.

Work, rights and corporate governance
- Real Living Wage of at least £10/hour for all 16+; ban zero‑hours contracts; day‑one rights; sectoral bargaining; ban unpaid internships.
- Target 32‑hour average full‑time week within a decade with no loss of pay.
- Create a Workers’ Protection Agency; require one‑third worker‑elected directors; Inclusive Ownership Funds in large firms.

Policing, justice and security
- Recruit additional police and PCSOs; restore neighbourhood policing.
- Reunify probation; restore legal aid; presumption against short prison sentences; strengthen victims’ rights.
- Overhaul cybersecurity; review border controls.

Housing
- Build over 1m social homes in a decade; at least 150k/yr by end of term, including 100k council homes; end Right to Buy.
- Rent controls; end no‑fault evictions; national licensing and standards; zero‑carbon homes standard; £1bn fire safety fund; end rough sleeping in five years.
- Create a Sovereign Land Trust; “use it or lose it” powers on stalled sites.

Digital, culture, media, sport, gambling
- Free full‑fibre broadband nationwide by 2030 via a public provider; Charter of Digital Rights.
- Cultural Capital Fund; arts premium; media plurality reforms; protect free TV licences for over‑75s.
- Football governance reforms; curb gambling advertising; new Gambling Act with limits and levy.

Migration, refugees, social security, equalities
- End hostile policies; end indefinite detention; close specified detention centres; protect family reunion; declaratory rights for EU nationals; safe routes and right to work for refugees.
- Replace Universal Credit; interim fixes (end five‑week wait and sanctions; scrap benefit cap and two‑child limit; raise Local Housing Allowance).
- Strengthen disability rights and benefits; increase Carer’s Allowance.
- Maintain pension triple lock; keep state pension age at 66; fair remedy for affected women; transparent pensions dashboard.

Constitution and governance
- Abolish the House of Lords, replacing it with an elected Senate after a constitutional convention.
- Votes at 16; automatic voter registration; repeal Fixed‑term Parliaments Act; stricter lobbying/donations rules; extend FOI.

Foreign policy and defence
- War Powers Act; increase diplomatic capacity; human‑rights‑led trade and arms export controls; climate diplomacy; recognise Palestine within a two‑state framework.
- Maintain NATO commitment and spend at least 2% of GDP on defence; renew the nuclear deterrent; support veterans; publish defence industrial and shipbuilding strategies.

Brexit
- Negotiate a customs‑union‑based deal with close single market alignment and put it to a confirmatory referendum alongside remain within six months; implement the result; guarantee citizens’ rights.

Summary of commitments and policies (ideological language removed; no parties or individuals named)

- Brexit and trade: Implement the negotiated exit, leave EU law, the single market and customs union; no extension of the implementation period beyond December 2020. Pursue a free trade agreement with the EU and new deals with the USA, Australia, New Zealand and Japan; aim for 80% of UK trade to be covered by FTAs within three years. Create up to 10 freeports. Maintain UK standards; the NHS not part of trade talks.

- Economy, tax and cost of living: No increases to the main rates of income tax, National Insurance or VAT; raise the NI threshold to £9,500 with an ambition for £12,500 tax-free income. National Living Wage to two-thirds of median earnings by 2024 (forecast ~£10.50). £1bn for childcare before/after school and holidays. Keep pensioner benefits including the triple lock. Tighten anti–tax avoidance (new HMRC unit, tougher penalties) and introduce a Digital Services Tax. Fiscal rules cap public investment at an average 3% of GDP.

- NHS and social care: Record funding uplift; 50,000 more nurses; 6,000 more GPs plus 6,000 other primary care professionals; 50 million more GP appointments a year. 40 new hospitals and 20 upgrades; Innovative Medicines Fund; mental health reform for parity of esteem; hospital parking concessions for those most in need. Fast-track NHS visa. Social care: at least £1bn extra per year, cross-party reform with a guarantee no one has to sell their home to pay for care; carers’ leave of one week; double dementia research funding.

- Education and skills: Additional £14bn for schools with minimum per-pupil funding; teacher starting salary to £30k; behaviour support; “arts premium”; more SEND funding and places. National Skills Fund (£3bn), FE estate upgrade (£2bn), 20 Institutes of Technology; UK Shared Prosperity Fund to replace EU funds (including £500m for disadvantaged people’s skills).

- Policing and justice: 20,000 extra police officers; targeted knife crime orders; tougher sentences and end automatic halfway release for serious crimes; 10,000 more prison places; cyber crime force and a National Crime Laboratory; review parole; Royal Commission on criminal justice; Victims’ Law; Domestic Abuse Bill; online safety legislation.

- Immigration: Australian-style points system; equal approach to EU and non‑EU; NHS and top talent fast-track routes; five-year qualification period for most benefits; higher health surcharge; stronger enforcement and integration (including English language).

- Housing: Support long-term fixed-rate mortgages; discounted homes for local people; maintain Right to Buy; extend Help to Buy to 2023; reform shared ownership and leasehold. End “no-fault” evictions and introduce a single “lifetime” tenant deposit. Target 300,000 homes a year by mid‑2020s; “infrastructure first” via a £10bn fund; building safety reforms; protect green belt; tree-lined new streets. End rough sleeping by end of Parliament; stamp duty surcharge on non‑resident buyers.

- Infrastructure and connectivity: Towns Fund, cultural and community ownership funds. Major rail upgrades (including Northern Powerhouse Rail and Midlands Rail Hub), rail reform, restoration of some Beeching lines, superbus networks and electric buses. £1bn rapid EV charging network; consult on earliest phase‑out date for new petrol/diesel cars. £350m cycling fund and universal Bikeability. Gigabit broadband nationwide by 2025 with £5bn for hard‑to‑reach areas. Minimum transport service during strikes.

- Business and innovation: Business rates review and cuts (retail, pubs, small cinemas, music venues); higher Employment Allowance; crackdown on late payments; expand start‑up loans. Increase SME R&D tax credit to 13%; review Entrepreneurs’ Relief; improve support for the self‑employed. Increase R&D to 2.4% of GDP, create a high‑risk research agency, invest in data/health research, science clusters, and a 2022 UK innovation festival.

- Rural, farming and fisheries: Replace CAP with “public money for public goods”; farm budget guaranteed during the Parliament; expand seasonal workers scheme to 10,000. Leave the Common Fisheries Policy, manage stocks sustainably, and support coastal regeneration. Improve rural broadband/mobile and buses; tackle rural crime.

- Environment and climate: Environment Bill with an independent watchdog; Nature for Climate Fund (£640m) for trees and peatland; new protected landscapes. Plastics measures, extended producer responsibility, deposit return scheme, ban most plastic waste exports. Net Zero by 2050; offshore wind to 40GW by 2030; first carbon capture cluster by mid‑2020s (£800m); £500m to decarbonise heavy industry; support hydrogen and nuclear (including fusion); fracking moratorium; £9.2bn for energy efficiency; stronger air quality laws; £500m Blue Planet Fund.

- Union, devolution and democracy: Strengthen devolution; UK Shared Prosperity Fund to at least match EU funding by nation; constitutional review via a Commission; repeal Fixed-term Parliaments Act; retain First Past the Post and voting age 18; voter ID and postal vote safeguards; restore full voting rights for UK expats; protect free speech (including media reforms).

- Defence, foreign policy and veterans: Exceed NATO 2% with 0.5% real annual growth; modernise forces, create Space Command, invest in cyber; maintain nuclear deterrent; support UK defence industry. New legal protections and support for veterans, NIC relief for employers hiring them, childcare, railcard, guaranteed public‑sector interviews. Maintain 0.7% aid; Magnitsky sanctions; promote girls’ education, media freedom, anti‑slavery; aim to end preventable maternal/child deaths by 2030; build the UK Holocaust Memorial.

- Animal welfare: Tougher cruelty sentences; crack down on puppy smuggling; animal sentience law; end excessively long journeys for slaughter; extend ivory ban; ban trophy imports and primates as pets; advance cat microchipping and measures against pet theft.
